chunks: Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad, from Muḥammad ibn ʿĪsā, from Ayyūb ibn Nūḥ, raising it, said:
There is no problem with salat (prayer) in pure khazz; but as for that in which rabbit fur or something else similar to this is mixed, then do not perform salat (prayer) in it.

key_terms.فَلَا تُصَلِّ: do not perform prayer; indicating prohibition in this context
key_terms.لَا بَأْسَ: there is no harm or objection; indicating permissibility
key_terms.وَبَرُ: fur or soft hair used as a clothing material
key_terms.ٱلصَّلَاةُ: the ritual prayer whose validity is being discussed
key_terms.ٱلْأَرَانِبِ: rabbits, whose fur is cited here as a disqualifying mixture in prayer garments
key_terms.ٱلْخَالِصِ: pure, unmixed with other disallowed substances
key_terms.ٱلْخَزِّ: khazz, a specific fabric material mentioned as permissible when pure

ai.seo_question: Is salat (prayer) valid in clothing made of pure khazz or mixed with rabbit fur?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling concerning clothing worn in salat (prayer). It permits salat (prayer) in pure khazz, while forbidding salat (prayer) in garments mixed with rabbit fur or similar materials.
